signals.context.convergence.actionableIn: Treat this as high-confidence intelligence; triangulation reduces false positive risk.
signals.context.convergence.confidenceNo: Very high confidence when wire + government + intel sources align.
signals.context.triangulation.whyItMatte: The "authority triangle" (wire services, government sources, intel specialists) are aligned—this is the gold standard for breaking news confirmation.
signals.context.triangulation.actionable: This is actionable intelligence; expect market/policy reactions imminently.
signals.context.triangulation.confidence: Highest confidence signal in the system—multiple authoritative sources agree.
signals.context.flow_drop.whyItMatters: Physical commodity flow disruption detected—supply constraints often precede price spikes.
signals.context.flow_drop.actionableInsi: Monitor energy commodity prices; assess supply chain exposure.
signals.context.flow_drop.confidenceNote: Confidence depends on disruption duration and alternative supply availability.
signals.context.flow_price_divergence.wh: Supply disruption news is not yet reflected in commodity prices—potential information edge.
signals.context.flow_price_divergence.ac: Either markets are slow to react, or the disruption is less significant than reported.
signals.context.flow_price_divergence.co: Medium confidence—markets may have better information than news reports.
signals.context.geo_convergence.whyItMat: Multiple news events clustering around same geographic location—potential escalation or coordinated activity.
signals.context.geo_convergence.actionab: Increase monitoring priority for this region; correlate with satellite/ship tracking data if available.
signals.context.geo_convergence.confiden: Higher confidence if events span multiple source types and time periods.
signals.context.explained_market_move.wh: Market move has clear news catalyst—no mystery, price action reflects known information.
signals.context.explained_market_move.ac: Understand the narrative driving the move; assess if reaction is proportional.
signals.context.explained_market_move.co: High confidence—news and price action are correlated.
signals.context.hotspot_escalation.whyIt: Geopolitical hotspot showing significant escalation based on news activity, country instability, geographic convergence, and military presence.
signals.context.hotspot_escalation.actio: Increase monitoring priority; assess downstream impacts on infrastructure, markets, and regional stability.
signals.context.hotspot_escalation.confi: Confidence weighted by multiple data sources—news (35%), country instability (25%), geo-convergence (25%), military activity (15%).
signals.context.sector_cascade.whyItMatt: Market movement is cascading across related sectors—indicates systemic reaction to a catalyzing event.
signals.context.sector_cascade.actionabl: Identify the primary catalyst; assess exposure across correlated assets.
signals.context.sector_cascade.confidenc: Higher confidence when multiple sectors move with similar velocity and direction.
signals.context.military_surge.whyItMatt: Military transport activity significantly above baseline—indicates potential deployment, humanitarian operation, or force projection.
signals.context.military_surge.actionabl: Correlate with regional news; assess nearby base activity and naval movements.
signals.context.military_surge.confidenc: Higher confidence with sustained activity over multiple hours and diverse aircraft types.

layerExplanation.layers.hotspots.purpose: Highlights monitored geopolitical hotspots and raises their level when related news and escalation signals converge.
layerExplanation.layers.hotspots.source: WorldMonitor hotspot registry, RSS/GDELT news intelligence, hotspot escalation scoring, military activity, and country instability context.
layerExplanation.layers.hotspots.freshne: Hotspot locations are curated/static. News feeds are freshness-tracked separately; hotspot levels are recomputed when the dashboard news feeds refresh, around 10 minutes apart, while GDELT intelligence has longer seeded/cache budgets.
layerExplanation.layers.hotspots.confide: Useful as a triage cue, not a citation-grade claim without opening the underlying news and country context.
layerExplanation.layers.hotspots.limitat: News volume and keyword matching can overrepresent highly covered regions.
Low-profile events may be missed when RSS/GDELT coverage is sparse or delayed.
layerExplanation.layers.no2Activity.purp: Colors countries and industrial clusters by the direction of their Sentinel-5P tropospheric NO2, a combustion trace, over the latest 56-day window against the same dates in prior years.
layerExplanation.layers.no2Activity.sour: Copernicus Sentinel-5P TROPOMI NO2 via the CDSE Sentinel Hub Statistical API, aggregated daily per region by the seed-no2-activity service. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data.
layerExplanation.layers.no2Activity.fres: Seeded every 24 hours; the window ends 3 days before the run so late granules can land, with a 72-hour freshness budget.
layerExplanation.layers.no2Activity.conf: A region reads only with at least 14 valid days and 2 baseline years; cloud cover is the dominant noise, so a thin window refuses a reading rather than guessing.
layerExplanation.layers.no2Activity.limi: Baseline pending is the expected state for weeks after a region is added, while prior-year windows are still being fetched.
NO2 tracks combustion, so cleaner generation or cleaner vehicles read as weakening activity.
layerExplanation.layers.conflicts.purpos: Shows curated conflict zones and geopolitical boundary overlays so analysts can orient live signals against known theaters.
layerExplanation.layers.conflicts.source: WorldMonitor conflict-zone registry, UCDP/ACLED conflict context, and documented boundary metadata such as the Korean DMZ.
layerExplanation.layers.conflicts.freshn: Base zones are curated/static. Dynamic conflict-event inputs are tracked separately through ACLED/UCDP feeds and health signals.
layerExplanation.layers.conflicts.confid: Good for geographic orientation; not a real-time incident confirmation by itself.
layerExplanation.layers.conflicts.limita: Static zones can lag fast tactical changes.
Some conflict evidence appears in conflict events, country instability, or related panels rather than as a conflict-zone polygon.
layerExplanation.layers.aircraftEmergenc: Shows reported transponder codes 7500, 7600 and 7700 independently of military classification.
adsb.lol exact squawk queries. Aircraft details use provider fields. Attribution is ODbL.
Checks each minute while visible. Last message must be at most 120 seconds old. Map positions must be at most 90 seconds old. Unknown reports expire after 15 minutes.
A reported transponder signal does not confirm an incident, cause, landing or resolution.
Last message time is not the time the squawk was selected.
Aircraft without fresh positions appear only in the details list.
Conflicts and loss of reception become unknown.
layerExplanation.layers.ais.purpose: Shows vessel density and AIS disruption signals around strategic waters and chokepoints.
layerExplanation.layers.ais.source: AISStream relay snapshots, WorldMonitor maritime service, and chokepoint disruption classifiers.
layerExplanation.layers.ais.freshness: AIS relay snapshots are rebuilt every 5 seconds by default; the server may cache the base density snapshot for 5 minutes, and the layer is disabled or stale when relay credentials/connectivity are unavailable.
layerExplanation.layers.ais.confidence: Useful for maritime anomaly screening, but AIS is self-reported and vessels can go dark.
Terrestrial AIS coverage is uneven, with weaker Middle East, Asia, and open-ocean visibility documented.
Dark shipping is inferred from gaps and congestion patterns, not direct proof of intent.
layerExplanation.layers.tradeRoutes.purp: Draws major container, energy, and bulk routes through strategic chokepoints for disruption-path reasoning.
layerExplanation.layers.tradeRoutes.sour: WorldMonitor trade-route registry plus supply-chain chokepoint status and transit summaries.
layerExplanation.layers.tradeRoutes.fres: Route geometry is static. Chokepoint status is warm-pinged every 6 minutes and transit summaries refresh every 10 minutes through supply-chain caches and relay paths.
layerExplanation.layers.tradeRoutes.conf: Good for route-level exposure context; not a ship-level routing feed.
layerExplanation.layers.tradeRoutes.limi: Routes are modeled corridors and may not match a specific voyage plan.
Disruption overlays depend on current chokepoint and AIS health.
layerExplanation.layers.flights.purpose: Highlights airport disruption and NOTAM closures, airspace NOTAMs in effect now or starting within 24 hours (temporary flight restrictions, restricted, danger and prohibited areas, military operating areas, airspace reservations and closures), and live aircraft positions when tracking is available.
layerExplanation.layers.flights.source: FAA ASWS, AviationStack, FAA NOTAM Management Service (NMS-API) and ICAO NOTAMs, adsb.lol (ODbL), Wingbits, legacy OpenSky service recovery, optional non-commercial airplanes.live/adsb.fi gap-fill, and the aviation service. Airspace NOTAMs are drawn as polygons where NMS supplies them, circles where the NOTAM gives a radius up to 250 NM, and markers otherwise.
layerExplanation.layers.flights.freshnes: Airport disruption seeds run on a 30-minute cadence; airspace NOTAMs are seeded every 5 minutes from NMS change pulls with a daily full resync, against a 20-minute freshness budget; the aviation panel also refreshes operational views on a 5-minute polling cycle.
layerExplanation.layers.flights.confiden: Best for disruption triage; individual live aircraft coverage depends on ADS-B availability and configured providers. NOTAM text is authoritative as distributed by the FAA.
layerExplanation.layers.flights.limitati: AviationStack-backed simulated demo data can appear when an API key is absent.
Live aircraft positions can be delayed or absent where ADS-B coverage is weak or blocked.
Airspace NOTAM areas are drawn on the deck.gl map only; the SVG and globe maps show airport markers.
Most US TFRs describe their shape only in text, so they appear as a marker at the NOTAM position, not as the restricted shape.
Schedules inside a NOTAM's effective window (for example daily hours) are shown in the tooltip but not applied to visibility.
layerExplanation.layers.ucdpEvents.purpo: Plots event-level armed conflict records with country, actors, date, and fatality ranges.
layerExplanation.layers.ucdpEvents.sourc: Uppsala Conflict Data Program GED API via the conflict service and UCDP event seed.
layerExplanation.layers.ucdpEvents.fresh: Seeded every 6 hours when the UCDP seed is healthy.
layerExplanation.layers.ucdpEvents.confi: Higher editorial consistency than raw breaking feeds, but intentionally lagging and not a live battlefield feed.
layerExplanation.layers.ucdpEvents.limit: Annual/research-grade release cadence can miss very recent events.
Fatality ranges are estimates and should be interpreted as ranges, not exact counts.
layerExplanation.layers.weather.purpose: Shows active official severe-weather alerts from national meteorological services, merged into one weather:alerts:v1 feed.
layerExplanation.layers.weather.source: United States National Weather Service (NWS), Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC), and WMO Severe Weather Information Centre (SWIC) CAP aggregation, seeded through the WorldMonitor relay.
layerExplanation.layers.weather.freshnes: NWS, ECCC, and SWIC alerts are seeded every 15 minutes by the relay and monitored against a 45-minute freshness budget.
layerExplanation.layers.weather.confiden: Authoritative for alerts issued by the contributing national services, subject to upstream publication timing. NWS and ECCC render as polygons; SWIC geocoded alerts render at the issuing service country centroid with an explicit precision marker.
layerExplanation.layers.weather.limitati: Most SWIC members publish geocodes, not polygons; those alerts appear as country-level points with the verbatim area description, not warned-area overlays.
SWIC coverage depends on which WMO members currently publish to the aggregator; density varies by region.
US and Canadian SWIC rows are skipped because NWS and ECCC already supply polygon-tier coverage for those countries.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaRoads.purp: Shows official road incidents, alerts, conditions, closures, construction, and hazards across supported Canadian jurisdictions.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaRoads.sour: Ontario 511, Alberta 511, and Manitoba 511 provincial feeds, City of Toronto Road Restrictions, and DriveBC Open511, seeded through WorldMonitor.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaRoads.fres: Ontario, Alberta, and Manitoba 511 are seeded every 15 minutes and monitored against a 45-minute freshness budget. Toronto restrictions are seeded every 2 hours; DriveBC Open511 every 30 minutes.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaRoads.conf: Authoritative for the supported provincial and municipal publishers, subject to upstream publication timing and mapped geometry.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaRoads.limi: Alberta 511 roadconditions is not ingested (the vendor endpoint 404s); live Alberta paint is events and alerts only.
Provincial alerts without coordinates do not appear as map dots.
Road-condition polylines may simplify complex highway geometry.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaAlerts.pur: Shows active Alberta, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan public-safety warnings as map dots alongside US NWS weather.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaAlerts.sou: Alberta Emergency Alert Atom, the OGL-BC Evacuation Orders and Alerts GeoJSON layer, and the SaskAlert public JSON feed plus same-host CAP 1.2 details are normalized into one canadaAlerts union. CAP/GeoRSS polygons, B.C. evacuation polygons, and SaskAlert CAP polygons become centroids; records without geometry use the source province centroid.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaAlerts.fre: Provincial sources are seeded every 15 minutes and the union is monitored against a 45-minute freshness budget. An empty feed (no active alerts) is a valid zero-record success.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaAlerts.con: Authoritative for alerts published by Alberta Emergency Alert, B.C. Evacuation Orders and Alerts, and SaskAlert, subject to upstream publication timing and mapped alert geometry.
layerExplanation.layers.canadaAlerts.lim: Coverage is limited to Alberta, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan. Ontario has no eligible province-operated machine feed outside excluded NAAD.
Does not replace US NWS weather alerts or Ontario/Toronto road layers.

Entries without a mappable severity (Alberta CAP/colour semantics, B.C. evacuation status, or SaskAlert CAP severity) are dropped rather than invented. SaskAlert summary colour/level is not treated as CAP severity.
layerExplanation.layers.cyberThreats.pur: Maps geo-enriched indicators of compromise such as C2 servers, malware hosts, phishing, malicious URLs, and ransomware infrastructure.
layerExplanation.layers.cyberThreats.sou: abuse.ch Feodo Tracker and URLhaus, C2IntelFeeds, AlienVault OTX, AbuseIPDB, ransomware.live RSS/news feed, and IP geolocation enrichment.
layerExplanation.layers.cyberThreats.fre: Cyber threat seeds run every 2 hours; displayed IOCs use a 14-day rolling window and are capped for map performance.
layerExplanation.layers.cyberThreats.con: Good for infrastructure visibility, but attribution and IP geolocation can be noisy.
layerExplanation.layers.cyberThreats.lim: IP geolocation can point to hosting infrastructure rather than an operator or victim.
Feed availability, API keys, and per-feed abuse reports can bias coverage.
layerExplanation.layers.natural.purpose: Shows earthquakes, severe disaster alerts, and active Earth-observation events for situational awareness.
layerExplanation.layers.natural.source: USGS earthquakes, GDACS alerts, and NASA EONET events merged into the natural events service.
layerExplanation.layers.natural.freshnes: Natural events are seeded every 3 hours; USGS earthquake expectations are documented at roughly 5-minute source cadence.
layerExplanation.layers.natural.confiden: Strong for detected public disaster signals; confidence varies by hazard type and upstream reporting latency.
layerExplanation.layers.natural.limitati: Low-severity GDACS alerts are filtered out to keep the map readable.
EONET wildfires are freshness-filtered, so older open events may not appear as active map points.
layerExplanation.layers.waterways.purpos: Marks strategic waterways and chokepoints so disruption signals can be interpreted against fixed maritime geography.
layerExplanation.layers.waterways.source: WorldMonitor strategic-waterways registry with supply-chain chokepoint status overlays from AIS, NGA warnings, and PortWatch-derived feeds.
layerExplanation.layers.waterways.freshn: Waterway locations are static; live chokepoint status is warm-pinged every 6 minutes and transit summaries refresh every 10 minutes when the relay/PortWatch path is healthy.
layerExplanation.layers.waterways.confid: High for fixed geography; live disruption confidence depends on the companion AIS, NGA, and PortWatch feeds.
layerExplanation.layers.waterways.limita: A visible chokepoint marker does not mean there is an active disruption.
Area geofences and modeled routes can simplify complex traffic patterns.
layerExplanation.layers.ciiChoropleth.pu: Colors countries by the current Country Instability Index score for broad strategic-risk triage.
layerExplanation.layers.ciiChoropleth.so: WorldMonitor Country Instability Index scoring service using conflict, unrest, advisories, cyber, ship tracking, aviation, natural-event, and news signals.
layerExplanation.layers.ciiChoropleth.fr: Risk-score cache is warm-pinged every 8 minutes; seed-meta and health.riskScores expose live, stale, partial, or degraded state against a 30-minute freshness budget.
layerExplanation.layers.ciiChoropleth.co: Composite model signal, not an official country rating or probability forecast.
layerExplanation.layers.ciiChoropleth.li: Sparse or degraded source families can reduce confidence even when a country still has a score.
Country-level color can hide subnational variation and should be checked against panels before citation.
layerExplanation.fallback.purpose: This layer can be toggled on the map, but a curated source and confidence card has not been added yet.
layerExplanation.fallback.source: Not curated in the v1 layer-explainability set.
layerExplanation.fallback.freshness: No layer-level freshness contract is declared here. Check the visible panel badges, popups, or data freshness status when available.
layerExplanation.fallback.confidence: Unknown until source-specific metadata is added.
layerExplanation.fallback.limitations.0: The lack of a curated card does not mean the layer is unsupported.
layerExplanation.fallback.limitations.1: Use layer popups and related panels for source-specific context.
